comparisons.comparison: Both firms disclose specific allowance and nonaccrual/nonperforming loan metrics for 2024, but they differ in granularity and asset classification. Goldman Sachs (GS) specifically isolates wholesale nonaccrual loans measured on an asset-specific basis, reporting $3.65 billion in such loans with a $735 million allowance and noting $585 million of these deemed recoverable without reserve. Bank of America (BAC) provides a broader total nonperforming loan figure of $6.0 billion for the same period but does not break out the specific asset-specific allowance or the recoverable portion within that total in the same manner. While both cover credit quality deterioration metrics, GS provides a detailed sub-component of its allowance methodology for nonaccrual assets, whereas BAC reports the aggregate balance sheet impact of nonperforming loans.

sentences.text: In the table above, wholesale loans included $3.65 billion as of December 2024 and $4.14 billion as of December 2023 of nonaccrual loans for which the allowance for credit losses was measured on an asset-specific basis.
The allowance for credit losses on these loans was $735 million as of December 2024 and $778 million as of December 2023.
These loans included $585 million as of December 2024 and $625 million as of December 2023 of loans which did not require a reserve as the loan was deemed to be recoverable.
Nonperforming loans were $6.0 billion and $5.5 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023.
